answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit bids or earn fees. Votes and rewards are weighted by locked stake, while proven fraud slashes that stake; splitting the same capital across a thousand accounts does not multiply influence. An attacker must acquire and immobilize substantial capital, risking its loss, and cannot cheaply mint identities on an island, cedar, or hollow network to overwhelm honest agents.
